text: Continuous integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, developers regularly add their code changes to a shared repository. This triggers automated builds, so the software is compiled and tested automatically every time someone makes a change. The CI pipeline then runs tests to check that everything works correctly. The main benefit is catching issues early. When a problem appears, it is much easier to find and fix it, because the change is still small. As a result, teams can deliver better software faster and with less stress.
